identity.source: Explicit payload-root Git only. A parent study repository is not searched.
identity.source_commit: HEAD is reported as commit only when a configured remote declares the expected public repository; any local HEAD is separately local_commit. The remote declaration is not upstream authentication.
identity.exact_commit: Matching declared remote, clean repository and all measured payload bytes equal Git blobs. This binds local bytes to a commit, not to a verified upstream release.
identity.dirty_snapshot: commit is a base; package_id and measured file identities describe the actual working snapshot.
identity.legacy: Retain null commit and rehash the old declared inventory. Do not infer commit from date, tag or directory name.
identity.snapshot_seal: Canonical SHA-256 metadata digest excluding package_id and observed_at_utc; payload_id hashes sorted measured file entries. These are integrity identifiers, not signatures.
identity.inventory: Public checkpoint or legacy guidance-freeze schemas only. Inventory self-entry is measured separately, avoiding recursive self-hashing.
identity.bounds: At most 10000 inventory entries, 32 MiB per file, 128 MiB total. Known method/tool/schema/entrypoint material omitted from inventory is rejected. Full release verification is still required for publication.

change_notes.append_only: An existing note cannot be deleted or edited across an update. Add a new superseding note instead.
change_notes.commit_link: Capture resolves introduced_commit for the note path from Git. An uncommitted new note has null introduced_commit. A historical backfill must separately state its original feature provenance; note introduction does not date the underlying feature.
change_notes.effect: New notes reappraise their paths even if target bytes are unchanged. Unchanged historical notes cannot index later unannotated changes.
change_notes.reading: Each affected review binds the current target, active note and all of that note's reading_paths to exact identities. reading_sections provide human anchors; actual full relevant-file reading is declared by the receiving agent.
change_notes.unindexed_material: Changed known material always becomes an explicit review; an absent note never silently accepts it. Other changed files remain in changes for study-level triage.

study_protocol.preserve_manifest: Study-root-relative path/bytes/sha256 entries. The checker validates only these explicit protected files; the tool never writes research files or automatically freezes an entire study.
study_protocol.revise_or_qualify: Reference newly derived artifacts and an existing acceptance_ref through the existing revisor workflow. Old results and old acceptance criteria remain attributed to their original package.
study_protocol.defer: The structural check remains unknown and pending. Continue unrelated authorized work under its recorded version; do not silently accept the affected gate.
study_protocol.activation: After impact appraisal and necessary revisor acceptance, record adopted package, declared study scope, effective time, responsible actor and next acceptance point. This tool does not write an active-version pointer.
study_protocol.reading_and_science: Required digest declarations establish referenced material identity only. Actual comprehension, scientific acceptance and revisor judgment require content review.
study_protocol.history: File delta is authoritative for legacy/dirty inputs. Even with exact commits, ancestry and whether to use a two-dot or other history comparison require separate Git inspection. No automatic pull, merge, rebase, rerun or history rewrite.

commands: python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out old.json capture --root OLD_PACKAGE
python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out legacy.json capture --root LEGACY_DELIVERY --inventory guidance-manifest.json --payload-prefix public-release --legacy
python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out new.json capture --root HARNESS_PUBLIC_ROOT
python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out received.json verify --root RECEIVED_PAYLOAD --snapshot new.json
python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out plan.json plan --old old.json --new new.json --preserve-manifest preserve.json
python tools/guidance_update.py --work-root STUDY_UPDATE_RECORDS --out checked.json check --study-root STUDY_ROOT --plan plan.json --receipt adoption.json

cli_rules.work_root: Create the intended records directory first; all output and input record names are canonical relative paths inside it. Capture output must be outside captured payload.
cli_rules.output: Exclusive new files only; existing outputs are rejected. Use a new run path to retain earlier records.
cli_rules.capture_or_plan_success: A generated plan remains pending study appraisal even though plan generation exits successfully.

decisions.reason: Explain applicability to current evidence and next decision.

git_and_feedback.default: Public Harness upstream plus separate private study history with a pinned dependency/package identity. Versioned folders work without Git metadata.
optional: same-repository worktree for local parallel development
avoid: copying private archive .git into a public payload
equating a study repository HEAD with Harness upstream HEAD
merging entire private research history as Harness feedback
assuming a worktree is automatically a named branch
feedback_unit: minimal observed failure or useful behavior
proposed general rule or scoped method card
git_and_feedback.research_outcome: Study progress and scientific findings stay in the study. Only curated reusable changes are proposed upstream.

validation.scope: Local source identity, change indexing, required-reading references, preservation and receipt structure.
